rationale:
What went well: The agent properly authenticated the user by matching full name and zip to a unique account. They looked up the correct order and product variants, and the chosen replacements matched the user's preferences. The computed price difference (+$17.61) aligns with the tool output.

Policy failures:
- No explicit confirmation before an order-changing write. The agent should have restated the exact changes (both items, variants, price difference, payment method) and obtained explicit confirmation before calling the exchange tool. Instead, they executed the exchange immediately after the user selected options.
- Unsupported/fabricated statement about modification being impossible. When the user asked to proceed only with the desk lamp and to hold off on the water bottle, the agent asserted the exchange "cannot be changed or cancelled" without consulting any tool or offering an escalation, contrary to policy which requires either using tools to check eligibility or handing off to a human if unsupported.

Because of these issues, the agent did not complete the request in line with the stated policy, despite correct identity verification and accurate pricing info.
